newsitem.title: USA: Two arrested, dynamite seized in U.S. bomb probe.
newsitem.headline: Two arrested, dynamite seized in U.S. bomb probe.

text.p: Police said they seized 500 pounds (230 kgs) of dynamite on Sunday and arrested two men suspected of carrying out bombings to subvert the justice system.

A joint federal-local task force was still searching for a third suspect in connection with two bomb attacks that rocked the town of Vallejo, 35 miles (50 kms) northeast of San Francisco, in the last week. A third bomb that was disarmed.
Vallejo police chief Robert Nichelini said police believed the bombers' aim was to "stop the criminal justice system from operating in Solano County," where Vallejo is located.

He said police believed the bombings were carried out in "an attempt to stop pending hearings," but he would not say if the suspects were involved in any criminal cases. The suspects acted together but were not "any sort of a militia group," he said.

Police found the huge haul of dynamite in a garage while searching a house in Vallejo on Sunday evening. "We located approximately 500 pounds of dynamite in individual sticks. That translates to about five or six cases of dynamite," Vallejo police Lieutenant Ron Jackson said.
Police ordered residents to evacuate nearby houses as a safety precaution while they removed the dynamite.

Vallejo police said they arrested one suspect, Francis Ernestberg, 40, at a house in Vallejo early on Sunday. He was booked into Solano County jail for investigation of conspiracy, explosives violations and burglary, they said.
Police also found a car with 61 sticks of dynamite in the trunk. The suspects were apparently planning to use the car in a bomb attack that could have been catastrophic, investigators said.
Later on Sunday, police arrested a second suspect, Oston Osotonu, 24, who was booked into jail on a no-bail warrant. He was charged with conspiracy and explosives violations, police said.

Police said they were still searching for a third suspect, Vallejo resident Kevin Robinson, 29, who is wanted on suspicion of conspiracy and explosives violations. They said he was considered armed and dangerous.
Police said the dynamite they recovered had been stolen. They believed they had found most of the missing dynamite.
Two bombs exploded in Vallejo in the last week, one outside a courthouse and one outside a bank. Both pre-dawn bombings caused damage but no injuries.
Last weekend, police also found and disarmed a bomb containing at least 30 sticks of dynamite that had been placed outside a public library that houses a police evidence room.

Paul Snabel, special agent in charge of the San Francisco office of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms, said the explosives found in the car on Sunday were "wired up and it was our understanding it was also to be used in a further attempt to subvert the justice system in Vallejo."
Snabel said the bombers apparently intended to drive the vehicle to a target and detonate it. Investigators said they did not know what the planned target was.
Nichelini said investigators believed the bank bombing may have been a diversion to throw the investigation off track and disguise the bombers' true motive.
